title: Design: verifiable agent identity, per-agent keys the other agents cannot read
description: Operator ratified 2026-09-23 (decision 4): gen-9 starts with a DESIGN, no code. Question: how can each agent hold a signing key the other agents cannot read, when every agent runs as the same OS user on one filesystem (D-17)? Survey what exists (OS keychains, per-agent OS users, hardware tokens, an external signer process holding keys on behalf of named agents, short-lived tokens minted by the operator). For each option: what it closes, what it leaves open, what the operator must run by hand, and a falsifier. State plainly if no option closes impersonation on 1 machine. Output: .harness/design-T-432-agent-identity.md. Do not touch trust/, constitutional/ or keys/. The operator approves the design before any worker task is created.
acceptance_criteria: A design document exists at .harness/design-T-432-agent-identity.md and cites D-17 as the standing limit.
Every option lists: what it closes, what stays open, what the operator runs by hand, and 1 falsifier a verifier can run.
The document states in 1 sentence whether any option closes impersonation on 1 machine.
No file under .harness/trust, .harness/constitutional or .harness/keys is read or written.
Handed off to a verifier; not self-marked done.
